newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian bourse sees trade booming on new listings.
newsitem.headline: Croatian bourse sees trade booming on new listings.

text.p: Croatia's central bourse expects to see a trading boom next spring after more companies from key branches list their shares, director Marinko Papuga said on Friday.

"The current market capitalisation of the 10 most active issues is $2.6 billion. They represent 14.6 percent of the gross domestic product," Papuga told an international conference on investment in Croatia.

He mentioned no names but said firms from food-processing and confectionery, tourism, shipping, telecommunications and the oil industry would probably float their shares in the coming 12 to 18 months.
To improve the supply of traded instruments, it is hoped that the government would also list more securities in addition to public debt refinancing bonds.
"We can expect a long-term development of the securities market, although there are still some problems," Papuga said, outlining missing infrastructure for clearing and settlement.
But he said all market institutions were working on a temporary solution, to be launched from January 1997, in a bid to cope with increasing trading demands.
Turnover this year has increased to over one billion kuna, boosted by the listing of Pliva and Zagrebacka Banka in the top stock bracket. -- Zoran Radosavljevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
